closing_words:
I'm filing six notices, most urgent window first. The figures and dates come from the Sitegrid, Dailylog and Estimato reads I did earlier. The markup is 15% on Corvane's own cost and 5% on the lower-tier cost. Each notice is a card for you to approve.


**What I left alone** (from the Dailylog, as I recorded it earlier)
- **15 Sept, conduit in the existing wing:** ED-101 shows it abandoned and says to leave it in place. That is the documents, not a change.
- **16–17 Sept, crew standby:** the window closed on 7 Oct. The event was before 18 Sept, so it is waived.
- **22 Sept, corridor D conduit:** this was our own error.
- **2 Oct, failed inspection:** this is our own rework.
- **5 Oct, copper price:** the price is fixed with no escalation clause.
- **PCO-22, PCO-27, PCO-36 and PCO-44:** already change orders or already noticed (NC-12).

**Caveat:** my recalled notes were cut off (20 of 55

trace.user: I'm worried we're letting changes slide on Westfold. Start here in Primeline GC: read the subcontract terms on claims, changes, markup and scope, and what's already been made a change order or noticed.
trace.said: I'll read the subcontract terms, the executed change orders and the notices already given.

Primeline is read. Here is what the terms say and what is already handled. The next step is Sitegrid, Dailylog and Estimato, which are other tabs.

**Terms**
- **Window:** 21 calendar days from the event, or from when Corvane first recognizes the condition, whichever is later. For an RFI answer, ASI, field directive or CCD, the event is the day of the direction.
- **Concealed conditions:** 14 days from first observation.
- **Waiver:** a claim not noticed in its window is waived (§11.3).

trace.user: Now Sitegrid: every RFI, ASI and directive that touches our work, and what each one actually tells us to do.
trace.said: I'll list the Sitegrid items, then open each one.
Nine items came back, and I'm opening each one. ASI-11 and ASI-13 already have a change order and a notice, but I'm reading them anyway to see what they direct.

Sitegrid has four open candidates for notice and one is urgent. RFI-60's window closes tomorrow, 10 Oct. Today is 9 Oct, so the window is open for events on or after 18 Sept.

| Item | Date | What it directs | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| RFI-60 | 19 Sept | GFCI at every break-room receptacle, rooms 118 and 214. E-301 shows standard receptacles. | **Candidate.** Window closes 10 Oct. |
| ASI-14 | 22 Sept | Add six duplex receptacles and one dedicated 20 A circuit in exam rooms 4 to 6.

trace.user: This is Dailylog. Read the foremen's entries since mid-September for anything that changed our work, and when.
trace.said: I'll read the foremen's entries from Dailylog now, starting with page 1.
Page 1 of 3 is read (5 of 13 entries). I'm fetching pages 2 and 3 now.

The Dailylog is fully read (13 of 13 entries). Two entries are new candidates, and the rest are leave-alone items.

**New candidates**
- **29 Sept, live circuits above corridor B.** The foreman meter-tested the old circuits and found three live, feeding the pharmacy refrigerators. ED-101 shows them abandoned, so this is a concealed condition. First observed 29 Sept, the 14-day window closes **13 Oct**.
- **1 Oct, temporary power.** Primeline's superintendent D.

trace.user: Now Estimato. Get the cost of every PCO, and any lower-tier sub in it.
trace.said: I'm reading the PCO list in Estimato now.
Page 1 of 2 is read (8 of 15 PCOs). I'm fetching page 2 now, then I'll open the PCOs for the open candidates, since the list may not show everything (notes, for example).
The list is complete: 15 of 15 PCOs. I'm opening the six that match open candidates to check their notes and the split between Corvane's cost and the lower-tier cost: PCO-31, 32, 33, 34, 35 and 43.

All six open candidates are priced. The markup is 15% on Corvane's own labor and material and 5% on the lower-tier sub's cost, per section 11.5. As a check, the same formula gives PCO-44 as $2,978.50, which matches the NC-12 notice already filed.
